test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the passage, what is the main focus of natural selection?

options.text: Ensuring the survival of the strongest individual organisms.
Promoting the good of the species as a whole.
Enhancing the survival and replication of genes.
Preserving the diversity of all living forms.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Selection at the Level of Replicators***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that **natural selection operates at the level of replicators—genes**—rather than individual creatures. The primary "goal" of this process is the survival and continuity of these genetic codes.
 
 
 
• ***The Gene-Centered View***
 
 
• The text explains that organisms (humans, ants, trees) are merely "temporary vehicles" or "survival machines" built by genes to ensure their own propagation. Therefore, the focus of selection is **enhancing the survival and replication of genes**.
 
 
 
• ***The Altruism Paradox***
 
 
• This focus explains why individuals might act altruistically; if an action helps related individuals who carry the same genes, it still serves the primary focus of **gene replication**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Enhancing the survival and replication of genes.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: Incorrect because the passage views individuals only as "temporary vehicles" for genes; the survival of the individual is secondary to the survival of the gene.
 
• **Option 2**: Incorrect because the passage specifically challenges this "anthropocentric tendency," stating that selection "cares nothing for abstract collective welfare."
 
• **Option 4**: Incorrect because while diversity exists in nature, the passage identifies the core mechanism of selection as the replication of successful gene variants, not the preservation of diversity for its own sake.
